A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SITCOM research. The complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support matching retained, relocated, revised, and added material.

before.justification: Section 4 and the appendices report original image-restoration experiments on FFHQ and ImageNet, including quantitative comparisons, ablations, and reconstructed images.

after.justification: Original restoration experiments remain, supplemented by latent-space, ODE, MRI, consistency-ablation, and noise-robustness results.

M1.justification: The core pixel-space Algorithm 1 remains, but Appendix E adds Latent-SITCOM with a decoder-composed measurement objective and latent-space resampling. Appendix F implements SITCOM-ODE, replacing the Tweedie reconstruction in S2 with an ODE solver. v1 mentioned the ODE replacement only as an unused possibility and listed latent sampling as future work.

E1.justification: The eight FFHQ/ImageNet restoration tasks remain. v2 adds fastMRI multicoil reconstruction with uniform and Gaussian undersampling masks, truly noiseless Gaussian deblurring, and Poisson-noise super-resolution/nonlinear-deblurring scenarios. These extend the domain and measurement conditions; the latent experiments themselves reuse existing dataset/task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated DMPlug and PGDM comparisons, ReSample and Latent-DAPS comparisons in Table 5, and MRI comparators including DDS, Score-MRI, E2E-VarNet, and TV-ADMM. v1 Table 3's DDRM and PnP-ADMM comparisons disappear. RED-Diff was already evaluated, but its participation changes from FFHQ/ImageNet nonlinear tasks to ImageNet SR, motion deblurring, nonlinear deblurring, and HDR.

E3.justification: The original restoration test sets, metrics, and main hyperparameter table are retained. New protocols include 8,000 training images for supervised MRI baselines and 50 MRI test images, latent-model evaluation, five-step ODE reconstruction, component-removal controls, and runtime comparisons using N/K adjustments to approximately match PSNR. The N/K and stopping-threshold sweep designs also expand.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds full-trajectory backward-consistency ablations and separate measurement- and forward-consistency tests, beyond v1's intermediate-image demonstrations. Appendices I–J add matched-quality timing analyses, convergence curves, threshold sensitivity, and Poisson-noise robustness. The original four-task N/K table is replaced in the PDF by a broader Gaussian-deblurring sweep; the regularization and stopping-on/off studies remain.

E5.justification: The retained RED-Diff ImageNet nonlinear-deblurring and HDR comparisons acquire standard deviations in v2 Table 1, whereas v1 Table 3 gives only sourced point estimates. The general mean-and-standard-deviation convention and best-of-four phase-retrieval procedure remain unchanged. No increase in repeated-run counts or new significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Many original image-quality values remain, but Table 1 reverses FFHQ phase-retrieval PSNR ordering: SITCOM/DAPS changes from 30.97/30.67 to 30.67/30.97. Reported runtimes also change beyond unit conversion: DCDP FFHQ super-resolution changes from 0.52 minutes to 19.10 seconds. Substantial new latent, ODE, MRI, ablation, and robustness results accompany removal of v1 Table 3's comparisons.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds Proposition D.1 and an approximation-based proof connecting K=1 SITCOM to DPS with resampling. This is a limited formal extension: the backward-consistency definition and Appendix A sampling derivation remain, and the broader acceleration argument is explicitly presented as heuristic rather than a performance guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion expand the demonstrated scope from natural-image restoration to medical reconstruction. The abstract replaces v1's significantly reduced runtime across all tasks with competitive or superior similarity metrics and runtime; Section 4.2 acknowledges faster baselines. This materially broadens applicability while qualifying the central efficiency claim. The triple-consistency contribution remains.

C2.justification: v2 adds an interpretation through grouped DPS updates and Adam, explains the cost of backpropagation versus fewer sampling steps, and discusses ODE quality/stability tradeoffs. v1's noise-estimation limitation is reconsidered using threshold-sensitivity evidence. Appendix B adds a 2D-only limitation and possible difficulties extending to 3D, while retaining the non-blind restriction.

D1.justification: New disclosures specify latent-model sources and hyperparameters, the Euler solver and five ODE steps, and MRI preprocessing, BART sensitivity estimation, pretrained-model sources, and sampling parameters. v2 explicitly identifies Adam as the experimental optimizer and adds links to extended ablations. Conversely, v1's explicit phase-retrieval oversampling-rate statement is omitted, without establishing a changed setting.

R1.justification: Section 3.2.1 newly positions backward consistency through CSGM generative priors. Relationships to DPS, RED-Diff, and DMPlug receive substantial additional treatment, and PGDM/MRI literature expands the comparison context. RED-Diff is reframed from computationally expensive to fast but limited in reconstruction quality and requiring an external denoiser. DDRM and PnP-ADMM references are removed.

P1.justification: The contribution narrative becomes an explicit list, the experimental discussion is substantially rewritten into Settings and Main Results, and detailed task descriptions move to Appendix K. Retained appendix material is reorganized around individual consistencies, comparisons, sensitivity studies, and implementation details. These structural changes accompany substantial new explanations, although much of the core method exposition remains.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column manuscript to the two-column ICML layout. Table 1 gains comparator rows, the conceptual schematic is revised, and new analysis tables, convergence plots, and MRI panels appear. The phase-retrieval montage gains SITCOM-ODE examples. v1's introductory FFHQ figure is relocated to Appendix L rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: Controlled consistency ablations and matched-quality timing comparisons substantially strengthen v1's support for its mechanism and efficiency claims. Threshold and Poisson-noise studies address practical robustness, while latent and MRI experiments replace proposed extensions with implemented evidence. These gains outweigh removed comparator coverage and reporting weaknesses. However, v2 still needs correction: its blanket latent-superiority statement conflicts with Table 5, and default runtimes differ without explanation between Table 1 and Tables 11–12.
